name: Sphinx, Androsphinx
body:
Mythic Androsphinx
CR 11/MR 4

This regal, bird-winged lion has a human’s head, clad in the golden raiment of a powerful pharaoh.

XP 12,800
CG Large magical beast (mythic)
Init +0; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +24

DEFENSE

AC 27, touch 9, flat-footed 27 (+18 natural, –1 size)
hp 163 (13d10+92)
Fort +12, Ref +8, Will +8
DR 10/epic

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor)
Melee 2 claws +20 (2d6+8/19-20 plus grab)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks mythic power (4/day, surge +1d8), pounce, rake (2 claws +20, 2d6+8), riddle of magicM, riddle of sand stone and skymma roarmma Spells Prepared (CL 10th; concentration +14)

5th—greater forbid action (DC 19), spell resistance
4th—aura of doom (DC 18), blessing of fervor, debilitating portentuc (DC 18), divination
3rd—bestow curse (DC 17), sands of time, searing light, speak with dead
2nd—bull’s strength, calm emotions (DC 16), cure moderate wounds, resist energy, silence (DC 16)
1st—comprehend languages, divine favor, endure elements, remove fear, shield of faith
0—detect magic, guidance, purify food and drink, stabilize

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 10, Con 18, Int 16, Wis 19, Cha 19
Base Atk +13; CMB +22; CMD 32 (36 vs. trip)
Feats Alertness, CleaveMF, Flyby Attack, Great Cleave, Hover, Improved Critical (claw), Power Attack MF
Skills Fly +5, Intimidate +14, Knowledge (any one) +16, Perception +24, Sense Motive +14, Survival +17
Languages Common, Draconic, Sphinx

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Riddle of Fate (Su)

As a swift action, a mythic androsphinx can choose two numbers, between 1 and 20. For 1 minute, whenever the result of a d20 roll made by a creature within 120 feet of the mythic androsphinx is one of these two numbers, it is treated as though it were the other number, instead. The mythic androsphinx can have multiple instances of this ability active simultaneously, but if it chooses the same number for two different instances of this ability, neither of them has any effect.

Riddle of Magic (Sp)

As a full-round action, a mythic androsphinx can expend a use of mythic power in order to attempt to cast a spell. The mythic androsphinx must choose a single spell of 7th level or lower from among the cleric, druid, and sorcerer/wizard spell lists, with a casting time of 1 round or less, and announce its intention to cast a spell, and invite any nearby creatures to guess what that spell is. The mythic sphinx must provide any three of the following pieces of information: the spell’s school and subschools, the spell list the mythic androsphinx is casting it from and the level at which it appears on that spell list, the spell’s range, or the spell’s components (including material components and focuses).

At any time before the beginning of the mythic androsphinx’s next turn, any creature can attempt to guess the spell. If a creature guesses correctly, it is rendered immune to the spell’s effect, as though by the spell spell immunity. Alternatively, when guessing, a creature can designate another creature to gain this immunity.

As a free action at the beginning of the mythic androsphinx’s next turn, it casts the spell as a free action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. For each creature that guessed incorrectly, the mythic androsphinx treats its caster level as 1 higher for the purposes of that spell (to a maximum of a +5 increase).

Riddle of Sand, Stone, and Sky (Su)

As a standard action, a mythic androsphinx can call out a riddle to all creatures within 60 feet, demanding to know which is the strongest: sand, stone, or sky. Each creature can choose to answer with one of these three. Then, roll 1d3 to determine which answer the mythic androsphinx chooses.

For the purposes of this riddle, sand beats stone, stone beats sky, and sky beats sand. Each creature gains a +2 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls made against characters who chose the answer that loses to their own. All creatures that chose an answer gain this bonus against creatures that chose note to give an answer, and such creatures do not gain any bonuses. These effects last for 10 minutes.

Roar (Su)

A mythic androsphinx can roar up to three times per day as a standard action. Each progressive roar has a different effect, depending upon whether it is the first, second, or third of the androsphinx’s roars for that day. All of these roars are sonic effects that fill a 60-foot-radius burst, centered on the androsphinx; the save DCs are Charisma-based. Sphinxes are immune to all of the effects of an androsphinx’s roars.

First Roar: Affected creatures become frightened for 2d6 rounds (DC 20 Will negates). Non-mythic creatures become panicked, instead. This is a mind-affecting fear effect in addition to being a sonic effect.
Second Roar: Affected creatures are paralyzed with fear and deafened for 1d4 rounds (DC 20 Will negates). Non-mythic creatures that fail their Will save also suffer a fear-induced heart attack, which inflicts 6d10 points of damage (DC 20 Fort negates). This is a mind-affecting fear effect in addition to being a sonic effect.
Third Roar: Affected creatures take a 2d4 penalty to Strength for 2d4 rounds, and take 4d8 points of sonic damage.

Creatures smaller than the androsphinx are knocked prone. A DC 20 Fortitude save negates the Strength penalty and being knocked prone.

By expending one use of mythic power, a mythic androsphinx can produce the effect of any of these three roars, even if it is not the first, second, or third time it has roared that day. This does not count against the androsphinx’s three daily uses of its roar ability, and does not count as a roar for the purposes of determining the effects of any further roars it makes that day.

Spellcasting

A mythic androsphinx casts divine spells as a 10th-level cleric.

They do not gain access to domains or other cleric abilities.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts or hills
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Among the mightiest of sphinxes, mythic androsphinxes (or “gizans,” as they often style themselves) see themselves as all that is worthy and noble in the species and carry themselves as though the weight of the world rests upon their good example. They view criosphinxes with condescension and hieracosphinxes with poorly veiled disgust and deem few but the wisest of other sphinxes worthy of their time. Gizans put on a gruff and cantankerous front to outsiders. They make no effort to hide annoyance when displeased but can be appeased with gifts and honor it feels are befitting of its station. Gizans tend to be territorial, though less so than other sphinxes. They almost invariably warn and bluster before attacking, and nearly always heed a call to parley.

Gizans barter information and conversation for safe passage, not treasure. Gizans are 12 feet tall and weigh 1,000 pounds.
